outages.cause: Rolling and emergency blackouts after Russian attacks on energy infrastructure
outages.affected: Ukrenergo said planned electricity outages would be in effect around the clock on Tuesday, Nov 17, in parts of Ukraine: capacity-restriction schedules for industry, and hourly outage schedules of 1 to 3 groups (queues) for all categories of consumers, because of the aftermath of attacks on the energy system. LB.ua, citing Ukrenergo, published that update at 10:18 p.m. EET Monday. UNN, citing Ukrenergo in an 8:07 p.m. EET Monday report, said one group equals four hours without electricity, so Tuesday's scheduled outages may last from 4 to 12 hours; it said up-to-date schedules should be checked on each region's distribution-system operator. On the evening of Monday, Nov 16, Ukrenergo said enemy strikes had caused large-scale power outages in eastern Ukraine and that the situation was particularly difficult in Dnipro, Kharkiv, Poltava, and Zaporizhzhia, where electricity supply was severely restricted because of significant damage to energy infrastructure. Ukrinform, citing Ukrenergo on Telegram, published that update at 7:30 p.m. EET. DTEK said the city of Dnipro was completely without power on Monday evening after an attack on energy facilities in the region (see the separate Dnipro row). As of the morning of Tuesday, Nov 17, Dnepr.info, in a 7:27 a.m. EET report, said electricity had been restored for some residents, but that scheduled stabilization outages had not yet been introduced in the hardest-hit areas; citing DTEK Dniprovski Elektromerezhi, it said emergency outages remained in effect, by Ukrenergo order, in parts of the cities of Dnipro, Kamianske, and Samar, as well as in the Samarivskyi and Dniprovskyi districts, Pavlohrad and the Pavlohrad district, and Solone and Tsarychanka, while scheduled stabilization outages were in effect in the rest of the region. Ukraine's Energy Ministry and First Deputy Minister of Energy Artem Nekrasov, as reported by Ukrainska Pravda at 2:14 p.m. EET Monday, said that after Russian attacks on Nov 16, parts of the Vinnytsia, Dnipropetrovsk, Kirovohrad, Odesa, Ternopil, and Cherkasy regions were left without power; they did not give customer counts for those regions. Pravda also reported Nekrasov as saying Russia attacked Ukraine's energy and oil and gas sectors 116 times during Nov 9–15, and that hourly power outage schedules were in effect across most regions of Ukraine, with capacity restriction schedules for industry. DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi said a Russian attack on the morning of Nov 16 on its facilities in the north of Odesa region left 52,200 households without power (see the separate Northern Odesa region row). No later official restoration figure for that outage was found. The Mykolaiv Regional Military Administration said Russian forces attacked the region's energy infrastructure on Monday evening with a Shahed-238-type drone, leaving 76 settlements in the Pervomaiskyi district without electricity. Mezha, citing a Mykolaiv Regional Military Administration briefing as of 7:30 a.m. EET Tuesday, Nov 17, said electricity had been restored to all 76 settlements (see the separate Pervomaiskyi district row). Cherkasyoblenergo, in an 8:58 p.m. EET Nov 16 statement, said that as a result of another attack, consumers in the Uman district were without power and that hourly outage schedules there temporarily did not apply; it gave no customer count. Ukrinform, citing the company, later reported the same. No later official Uman restoration figure was found. On the Nov 15 Zaporizhzhia attack, Zaporizhzhiaoblenergo, as reported by Interfax-Ukraine, said electricity supply to 359,000 consumers in Zaporizhzhia and the region was disrupted and that after critical infrastructure was restored in 4.5 hours, power was returned to 359,000 households and legal entities a few hours later; Mykhailo Semikin, acting head of the Zaporizhzhia Regional Military Administration, had said Sunday evening that power supply had been restored in the Zaporizhzhia region, according to Ukrinform at 9:00 p.m. EET Sunday. Ukrenergo's Monday evening update again listed Zaporizhzhia among the cities where supply was severely restricted; it did not give a new customer count. Overnight Nov 15 outages: DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi said in a Nov 15 statement that a Russian attack overnight on one of its energy facilities left 41,000 customers without power (no later official restoration figure found; see the separate Odesa region, including Chornomorsk, row). Sumyoblenergo, in a Nov 16 update reported by SUMYTODAY, said part of Sumy region was still without a stable electricity supply for a second day after an accident at a high-voltage facility (no customer count); no later official update was found. On Friday, Nov 13, Chernihivoblenergo said an attack left about 150,000 customers without power in the Nizhyn and Pryluky districts; no later Chernihiv customer figure or confirmed restoration was found. A Nov 16 DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi statement said that from Nov 9 to 15, crews restored power to 306,100 families in 637 villages and towns in the Odesa region; that weekly total does not give a later official figure for the morning Nov 16 northern Odesa outage or the overnight Nov 15 outage. In Russian-occupied parts of the Donetsk region, occupation authorities said 428,000 subscribers remained without electricity on Monday evening and that most previously de-energized consumers had been reconnected by Tuesday morning, with emergency outages still occurring (see the separate occupied Donetsk region row).

outages.cause: Russian attack on energy facilities in the region
outages.affected: No official customer count. As of the morning of Tuesday, Nov 17, the citywide Monday-evening blackout was no longer in effect for the whole city, but emergency outages continued in parts of Dnipro and nearby areas. Dnepr.info, in a 7:27 a.m. EET Tuesday report, said electricity had been restored for some residents, but that scheduled stabilization outages had not yet been introduced in the hardest-hit areas. Citing DTEK Dniprovski Elektromerezhi, it said emergency outages remained in effect, by Ukrenergo order, in parts of the cities of Dnipro, Kamianske, and Samar, as well as in the Samarivskyi and Dniprovskyi districts, Pavlohrad and the Pavlohrad district, and Solone and Tsarychanka, while scheduled stabilization outages were in effect in the rest of the region. Informator, also citing DTEK Dniprovski Elektromerezhi, reported the same emergency-outage list for Tuesday. On Monday evening, DTEK, in a Telegram statement reported by Interfax-Ukraine at 6:59 p.m. EET and Ukrinform at 7:08 p.m. EET, said that after an attack on energy facilities in Dnipropetrovsk region, the city of Dnipro was completely without power, and that some residents of the Dniprovskyi, Samarivskyi, and Kamianskyi districts were also without electricity. DTEK said crews were already restoring supply, returning power first to water and heating systems and social facilities, and warned that further Russian attacks could slow the work. Dnipro Mayor Borys Filatov, in a Monday Telegram post reported by NV at 7:10 p.m. EET, said that after Russian attacks on the city, almost half of Dnipro was without electricity, and he called it the sixth blackout in two weeks. He also said two people were killed, eight were in hospital, and 10 apartment buildings were damaged. Ukrenergo, as reported by Ukrinform at 7:30 p.m. EET Monday, said the situation was particularly difficult in Dnipro, Kharkiv, Poltava, and Zaporizhzhia, where electricity supply was severely restricted because of significant damage to energy infrastructure. No official customer count or time for full restoration of the remaining emergency outages was found.

outages.cause: Russian attack on DTEK energy facilities
outages.affected: 52,200 households without power, according to a Nov 16 statement by DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi. DTEK said a Russian attack on the morning of Nov 16 hit its energy facilities in the north of Odesa region, that 52,200 households were temporarily left without electricity, that specialists were inspecting surviving equipment in order to begin repairs as soon as possible, and that all work is being carried out under safety rules, including during air-raid alerts. DTEK also said the company's production site was damaged in the attack (windows blown out and ceilings and doors damaged) and that employees were not injured. No restoration time was given. This is a separate, later attack in the north of the region from DTEK's Nov 14 statement that a morning attack on one of its facilities there left almost 50,000 customers without power, and from the overnight Nov 15 DTEK attack that left 41,000 households without power in the Odesa region. A Nov 16 DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi statement said that from Nov 9 to 15, crews restored power to 306,100 families in 637 villages and towns in the region; that weekly total does not give a later official figure for this morning Nov 16 outage. No later official customer count or restoration notice was found after the morning Nov 16 statement.

outages.cause: Russian attack on a DTEK energy facility
outages.affected: 41,000 customers without power, according to a Nov 15 statement by DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi. DTEK said a Russian attack overnight on Nov 15 hit one of its energy facilities, that 41,000 customers were left without electricity, that crews began work once it was safe, that specialists were inspecting surviving equipment, clearing rubble, and making repairs, that restoration will take a long time, and that air-raid alerts were significantly complicating the work. No restoration time was given. Oleh Kiper, head of the Odesa Regional Military Administration, said around 41,000 customers were temporarily left without electricity after a strike on a DTEK Odesa Electricity Networks facility. Ukraine's State Emergency Service said Russia attacked Chornomorsk; reporting on the same overnight attack said the city was left without power and that six people were injured. This is a separate outage from the morning Nov 16 DTEK attack in the north of Odesa region that left 52,200 households without power. A Nov 16 DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi statement said that from Nov 9 to 15, crews restored power to 306,100 families in 637 villages and towns in the region; that weekly total covers Nov 9–15 and does not give a later official figure for this overnight Nov 15 outage. No later official customer count or restoration notice was found.

outages.cause: Russian Shahed-238-type drone attack on energy infrastructure
outages.affected: No official customer count. The Mykolaiv Regional Military Administration said Russian forces attacked the region's energy infrastructure on Monday evening, Nov 16, with a Shahed-238-type drone, leaving 76 settlements in the Pervomaiskyi district without electricity, and that power restoration work was underway. Ukrinform published the Ukrainian report at 8:37 p.m. EET Monday. Interfax-Ukraine, citing the regional administration head, Georgiy Reshetilov, on Telegram, reported the same figures at 8:41 p.m. EET. Mezha, citing a Mykolaiv Regional Military Administration briefing as of 7:30 a.m. EET Tuesday, Nov 17, said electricity had been restored to all 76 settlements and that there were no casualties from that attack. No official customer count was given.
outages.etr: Restored as of 7:30 a.m. EET Tuesday, Nov 17, according to Mezha, citing a Mykolaiv Regional Military Administration briefing

outages.place: Mariupol, Donetsk, Volnovakha, Novoazovsk, and nearby cities
outages.cause: Occupation authorities said energy infrastructure was attacked on the nights of Nov 15 and Nov 16, causing an emergency in the regional power system. On Nov 15, the Russia-appointed head of the Donetsk occupation government, Andrey Chertkov, said the grid was damaged by a "powerful enemy attack," while some Russian media called it an accident. Vedomosti reported that Ukrainian forces struck energy infrastructure in the region overnight Nov 15
outages.affected: Occupation authorities have not given a single independently confirmed total, and the latest official figures they issued still come from occupation sources. Donetsk Agency News (DAN), in an 8:30 p.m. local Nov 16 report, citing the occupation administration of the head and government of the occupied Donetsk region and Donetskenergo director Oleg Pavlyak, said 428,000 subscribers remained without electricity. Of those, it said 284,000 were de-energized because of the emergency shutdown of a power unit, and 144,000 household consumers were under a temporary capacity-limitation schedule (GVO) of 95 MW. It said the unit was expected to start by midnight, after which specialists planned to begin restoring supply to consumers in Donetsk, Mariupol, and the Novoazovsk, Volnovakha, and Novotroitsk districts. News-donetsk.ru, in an 8:14 a.m. local Tuesday, Nov 17 report citing the occupation Ministry of Coal and Energy, said energy workers had carried out the necessary restoration work and that most previously de-energized consumers had already been reconnected. It said the regional power system remained under strain, that because of a shortage of available capacity and high grid load, forced temporary outages were possible in Donetsk, Horlivka, and Yasynuvata, and that local outages were also occurring in Makiivka, Yenakiieve, Novoazovsk, and Shakhtarsk municipal districts. It said the outages were emergency in nature, were not planned in advance, and were introduced based on the current state of the grids and the load; it did not give a new customer count. Earlier Monday morning figures, which have been superseded by the later Monday evening and Tuesday morning updates, included 201,220 subscribers without electricity in all districts of Donetsk, according to occupation-appointed mayor Alexey Kulemzin citing Donetskenergo, as reported by news-donetsk.ru at 10:55 a.m. local Nov 16, and more than 133,500 subscribers without electricity in Mariupol, with 941 transformer substations in the urban district still de-energized, according to the occupation administration of the Mariupol urban district as reported by MRPL.NEWS at 9:41 a.m. local Nov 16. These figures come from occupation authorities and were not independently confirmed in the sources reviewed. No later official customer count after the Tuesday morning qualitative update was found.

outages.cause: Generation capacity deficit, with several thermoelectric units offline due to breakdowns and maintenance. UNE's Monday bulletin, published by Cubadebate, said that at 6:00 a.m. Monday, unit 8 of CTE Mariel, unit 1 of CTE Santa Cruz, the Antonio Guiteras unit, and unit 2 of CTE Felton were in breakdown, and that unit 3 of CTE Santa Cruz, unit 5 of CTE Nuevitas, unit 1 of CTE Felton, and unit 5 of CTE Renté were in maintenance; thermal generation was also limited by 281 MW
outages.affected: UNE's Monday bulletin, published by Cubadebate, is the latest official national forecast found: 1,760 MW affected at the evening peak, with 1,070 MW available versus 2,800 MW demand (1,730 MW deficit), if the forecast conditions hold. At 6:00 a.m. Monday, the grid had 870 MW available versus 2,070 MW of demand, leaving 1,186 MW unserved, and UNE estimated 1,400 MW affected at midday. UNE said the Guiteras unit was expected to add 180 MW and unit 6 of Nuevitas a further 20 MW at the Monday evening peak. On Sunday, service was affected by a generation-capacity deficit for all 24 hours and remained affected through the early morning; the maximum Sunday affectation was 1,874 MW at 7:00 p.m. Sunday. Sunday solar photovoltaic output was 3,827 MWh, with a maximum of 595 MW at midday. CiberCuba, in a Monday report, said the Antonio Guiteras plant synchronized with the National Electric System on Monday after five days of emergency repairs, after going offline on Wednesday, Nov 11; it said the return was not enough to close the deficit. CiberCuba, citing the Empresa Eléctrica de Las Tunas, later said the province was disconnected from the National Electric System at 6:02 p.m. Monday because of a system emergency; it did not give a customer count or a reconnection time. CiberCuba, citing the Empresa Eléctrica de La Habana, said that at 6:00 p.m. Monday the capital had 144 distribution circuits affected by a generation deficit, with 335 MW affected. No official Monday evening-peak national actual from UNE was found, and no Tuesday, Nov 17, UNE national bulletin had been published yet at the time of this check. Official UNE and Cubadebate sources did not report a total collapse of the national grid.

outages.place: Mayfair West, Amalgam, Vrededorp, Pageview, and nearby Johannesburg suburbs
outages.cause: Fire and a later explosion at the Mayfair substation; after a Thursday-night restoration, the Hursthill substation tripped early Friday because of a network overload. City Power later said the first explosion was caused by cable theft. A separate Crown Substation fault and a Florida Glen cable theft also interrupted supply. On Sunday, City Power said a 16-hour emergency shutdown was needed to complete critical Mayfair Substation repairs
outages.affected: No official customer count. SABC News, in a 10:01 a.m. SAST Monday, Nov 16 report, quoted City Power spokesperson Isaac Mangena saying that restoration shortly after midnight had brought several critical customers and sections of the network back online, including the SABC and Netcare Garden City Hospital, and that restoration work was continuing. He said parts of Crown remained outstanding and were scheduled to receive attention on Monday, and that technicians were also attending to further cable faults affecting customers in Mayfair West, Amalgam, Vrededorp, Homestead Park, and Pageview, among others. eNCA, in a noon SAST Monday report attributing the update to City Power, said electricity had been restored to the SABC, Netcare Garden City Hospital, and approximately half of Crown's industrial area, that residents and businesses in Mayfair West, Amalgam, Vrededorp, and Pageview remained without electricity because of ongoing cable faults, and that power to Sentech remained switched off for further maintenance and safety checks. No official restoration time for the remaining areas or for Sentech was given. Earlier Monday, City Power's Hursthill SDC bulletin issued at 7:30 a.m. SAST did not list the Mayfair Substation 16-hour emergency shutdown among current outages. In a Sunday, Nov 15, Mayfair Substation customer alert posted at 12:15 p.m. SAST, City Power said it would implement a 16-hour emergency shutdown from 12:00 noon Sunday to complete critical repairs at the Mayfair Substation; the planned window would have run until 4:00 a.m. SAST Monday. The same Monday 7:30 a.m. Hursthill bulletin said the centre was managing 1,524 open calls, 1,266 of them more than 24 hours old (a wider Hursthill service-area figure, not a customer count for the Mayfair outage alone). It also reported other Hursthill-area outages, including an investigation in Coronationville, Westbury, Newclare, and Paarlshoop (reported Sunday, no customer count); the Roosevelt Substation (Emmarentia Distributor) outage, about 75% restored, with customers particularly along Barry, Hertzog, and Muirfield remaining off until repairs were complete; and Industria Substation outages. In a 7:35 a.m. SAST Monday Roodepoort SDC bulletin, City Power said one load centre at Florida Substation would remain off until repairs were completed for customers in Florida Lake, Hamberg, and Georginia, and that loadshedding remains suspended until further notice. No later official City Power restoration notice for the remaining Mayfair-area suburbs, parts of Crown, or Sentech was found after the Monday midday reports.
outages.etr: No official restoration time was given for remaining Mayfair-area customers, parts of Crown, or Sentech. For the Roosevelt Substation outage in parts of Emmarentia, City Power said Monday morning that repairs were scheduled that morning and that customers particularly along Barry, Hertzog, and Muirfield would remain off until repairs were complete. For the Florida Lake, Hamberg, and Georginia outage, City Power said Monday morning that one load centre would remain off until repairs were completed and gave no restoration time.

outages.cause: Drone attacks on power stations and other electricity infrastructure during the war between the Rapid Support Forces and the Sudanese Armed Forces
outages.affected: No official customer count. Al Jazeera, in a Nov 15 report, said the RSF has intensified attacks on power stations around Khartoum state over the past month, creating an energy crisis in the capital, and that there is no clear schedule for the resulting power cuts, which can last anywhere between six hours and a day. It said that between Oct 20 and Nov 2, 2026, there were at least 18 attacks on electricity infrastructure across at least nine states, leading to declining power generation capacity and fuel shortages. Citing The Associated Press, it said repeated drone attacks on power stations have seen electricity generation fall from about 4,400 megawatts before the war to about 1,100 MW today. Residents and a small-business owner in Port Sudan described prolonged, unreliable cuts, including outages lasting more than 24 hours. The UN resident and humanitarian coordinator, Denise Brown, was quoted warning that repeated strikes on power and fuel stations were disrupting dialysis, hospital births, and operations. No later official national customer count or restoration timetable was found.
outages.updated: Nov 15, 2026 (Al Jazeera feature, published Nov 15); generation figure attributed to The Associated Press; rechecked 11:55 PM CT Monday, no later official national customer count or restoration timetable found
